hypothesis: The recurring subgroup is detectable, but a 32-center callable does not reconstruct its nonlinear response on disjoint states. Additional response locations may help; disagreement-guided locations should outperform equal-count random locations if the retained callable ensemble contains useful acquisition information.
world: new opened-development world only; no confirmation
generator: 4D hidden P3 callable recurrence plus system-specific linear maps; eight of sixteen acquisition systems selected is a supplied capacity choice, not discovered cardinality
allowed_access: controlled resets and one-step responses at chosen states for acquisition systems; target systems still provide exactly 32 controlled context transitions
selection: eight leave-one-selected-system-out RBF callables fitted on the initial panel; greedy score equals output disagreement times distance from already selected support; 16 states; no candidate response is read before indices persist
controls: random and adaptive receive equal extra responses, kernel centers, coefficient solve, target context and query bank; original32 isolates more-data effect
retained_knowledge: per arm, callable centers and 4-vector RBF weights; 256 scalars at 32 centers or 384 at 48 centers
per_target_inference: 16 linear coefficients plus one callable coefficient from 32 observed transitions
qualification: This is an engineered controlled-probe support diagnostic. It changes information cost, uses heuristic disagreement rather than calibrated uncertainty, and does not establish passive inference or open-ended dynamics discovery.
